instructions: Chop 1 of the onions as fine as you can. Squeeze it in your fist over the sink to get rid of the juice.
Pick the leaves off the parsley and chop them. You want 1/2 cup.

Put the 1.25 lb ground beef in a large bowl with the squeezed onion, 1/4 cup of the parsley, 1 tsp of the allspice, the 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper. Mix it with your hands until it comes together. Stop as soon as there are no streaks left. Any longer and the meatballs come out dense.
Roll the mixture into balls about the size of an apricot. That should be about 24. Set them on a plate.
Cut the other 2 onions in half and slice them thin. Dice the 3 tomatoes.

Heat the 1/4 cup oil in a wide, deep frying pan that has a lid, over medium heat. Add the 1/3 cup pine nuts and stir them the whole time until they're golden, 2 to 3 minutes. Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto a small plate. Watch them closely. They go from golden to burnt in seconds.

Turn the heat up to medium high. Add half the meatballs with room between them and leave them alone for about 1 minute, until the underside is brown. Turn them and keep going until they're browned all over, about 5 minutes in all. Transfer them to a plate and brown the rest the same way. They'll still be raw in the middle, and that's fine.
Turn the heat down to medium and add the sliced onions to the same pan. Cook them, stirring now and then, until they're soft and golden at the edges, about 8 minutes.

Meanwhile, start the rice. Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Melt the 1 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat, add the rice and stir for 1 minute, until every grain is coated.
Add 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt to the rice and bring it to a boil. Turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and keep the lid on until you serve.

Back at the onions, add the 1 tbsp tomato paste, the rest of the allspice (1/2 tsp) and the rest of the pepper (1/4 tsp). Stir for about 1 minute, until the paste turns a shade darker and the spices smell warm.
Add the tomatoes and the last 1/2 tsp salt. Cook, stirring, until the tomatoes soften and start to break down, about 5 minutes.
Pour in 2 cups water and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring it to a boil.
Put the meatballs back in the pan in one layer, with any juice from the plate. Turn the heat to low, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sauce has thickened a little.
You're cooking the meatballs to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one in half: it's done when there's no pink left.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Spoon the meatballs and sauce over the rice and scatter the pine nuts and the rest of the parsley over the top.
method_notes: All three brown allspice-seasoned meatballs, then simmer them in a tomato sauce built on onion and serve them over rice. Hadia's Lebanese Cuisine keeps it plain with sliced onions, fresh tomato, a little tomato paste and toasted pine nuts stirred in at the end, and suggests pomegranate molasses at the table; But First Chai adds cinnamon, potato and bell pepper and cooks the molasses into the sauce; Recipes Are Simple goes richer with ghee, cardamom and cloves and serves saffron rice. This one follows Hadia's method, borrows the cinnamon and stirred-in pomegranate molasses from But First Chai, and leaves out the cayenne so the pot stays mild. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats has no version, so Hadia's leads as the classic Lebanese one.
